title: Rumania
identity: Rumania (1979) is one of three early jazz-inspired works composed or arranged for saxophone by David Heath; a 2020 DMA dissertation provides a performer’s guide and analysis to Rumania alongside Out of the Cool and Coltrane. A contemporary 1988 review describes the work as one movement with contrasting lyrical/rhapsodic and quicker jazz-influenced sections and notes a soprano-sax part was separately available. The original David Heath work is for violin and piano; the saxophone edition is an arrangement, so distinguish the exact sax version from later retailer listings.

evidence.claim: The University of Nebraska–Lincoln repository identifies the 2020 DMA dissertation, its three titles, composer-arranged saxophone repertoire, and its analysis/performance-guidance scope.
Dissertation record describes the works as early jazz-inspired saxophone repertoire by a British composer.

Publisher identifies Heath’s Rumania as a 1979 work originally for violin and piano, written for Nigel Kennedy, with episodic sections and jazz/Bartók inspiration. It does not list the saxophone version on this page.

A 1988 review states that a soprano saxophone part is available separately and describes the single-movement work as alternating lyrical/rhapsodic and faster jazz-influenced sections; the reviewer considers it suitable for competent amateurs or experienced students. This is contemporaneous review evidence, not a saxophone score inspection.

review_focus: Inference from the 1988 review: contrast long lyrical/rhapsodic phrasing with quicker jazz-influenced sections; score-level articulation, range, and sax-specific technique remain unknown.
collection_flag: Saxophone arrangement of a work originally composed for violin and piano. Contemporary review and later dissertation discuss its saxophone performance; not evidence that the sax part is a literal violin transcription.

score_links.description: Repository record links to dissertation; score was not inspected.
